channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-14
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 157 news received.

item.title: 1. Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Why it matters: Jensen Huang’s reported departure from Nvidia would be a major leadership and market shock, with potential consequences for the AI-chip ecosystem and Nvidia’s valuation. Jensen Huang has reportedly resigned as Nvidia’s CEO following reports of two alleged affairs with Chinese spies. Nvidia’s valuation fell by $800 billion after the controversy.

item.title: 2. A Global Microsoft 365 Outage Affects Outlook and Teams
item.description: Why it matters: The global Microsoft 365 outage highlights the operational and concentration risks businesses face when core email, collaboration and AI services depend on one cloud provider. A global Microsoft 365 outage disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and other services. Microsoft attributed it to an overloaded secure-connections process and said it was not a cyberattack.

item.title: 3. Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Coding Assistants
item.description: Why it matters: Google’s Gemini 4 Hydrogen strengthens competition in coding and tool-using AI, potentially affecting developer workflows, model economics and enterprise adoption. Google has launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a model designed for coding assistants and software that uses tools. It accepts text, images, audio, and video, with adjustable reasoning levels and usage-based pricing.

item.title: 4. Companies are divided over AI agents’ access to commerce
item.description: Why it matters: Companies are now making strategic decisions about whether and how AI agents may access commerce, shaping the next distribution layer between businesses and customers. Amazon, Booking.com, eBay, Target, Resy, Yelp, and other companies are taking different approaches to third-party agents, ranging from blocking them to approving certain platforms. Companies will therefore choose where and how they participate in the agentic web.

item.title: 5. Google Unveils Intelligent Eyewear, the Successor to Google Glass
item.description: Why it matters: Google’s new Gemini-powered smart glasses signal a renewed race to make ambient AI a mainstream consumer interface beyond phones and computers. These new smart glasses let users use Gemini in everyday life to ask questions, take photos, and translate conversations. Preorders are open, and deliveries will begin on December 10.
